armF.prompt:
Below is a finished English news feature article (already translated from Japanese, no section headings). Write ONE short, natural sentence that captures the core of the story, in a way a listener can understand by hearing it just once.

Requirements:
- Exactly one sentence.
- Understandable on a single listen.
- Do not pack in multiple separate points; focus on the single most important point or twist of the story.
- Do not add any new fact, conclusion, or lesson that is not already stated in the article below.
- Keep who did what to whom, and what exactly it applied to, the same as in the Japanese source article and the Ledger below.

As a rough guide only (Trial-only guidance, not a strict rule): aim for one main clause with at most one subordinate clause, roughly 12-18 words.

Output only the sentence itself, nothing else (no quotation marks, no label like "In one line:", no Markdown heading markup).

[Article]
# The Star of Space Weapons News Is Where the Weapons Are

When you hear “weapons in space,” you may imagine a movie scene. But this time, the weapon’s address matters most. Is it on the ground, or is it in orbit? If we get this wrong, the same space news may tell a different story.

On September 14, 2026, the US Secretary of the Air Force spoke about space-control weapons in orbit. The United States was deploying them to protect the joint force from hostile parties. An official US government article called this the first statement confirming the Space Force had put weapons into space. But we still do not know the exact system, its attack ability, or its targets.

From here, we have a sorting game about space weapons. Let’s turn over three cards.

The first card shows a ground-launched anti-satellite missile. In 2021, Russia used a missile to destroy a satellite. This created more than 1,500 pieces of space debris that people could track. It was a major event. But it was a test from the ground against a satellite. Its address was different from the address in this announcement about orbiting weapons.

The second card says “counterspace.” This does not only mean weapons put in space. In the US Space Force’s framework, it means attacks and defenses in orbit. It also covers communication links and ground facilities. The term includes electromagnetic interference and cyberattacks too. So, even with “space” in its name, the weapon may not be in space.

The third card shows defensive systems. They warn about threats and make satellites harder to destroy. They also spread out functions and satellites. They keep backup systems as well. These protections are different from attack weapons in orbit. Still, active defense can sometimes include weapons. Our lives depend on satellite communication and positioning. So, this sorting is not only about distant space.

Finally, we have the rulebook: the Outer Space Treaty. Article 4 bans nuclear weapons and other weapons of mass destruction in Earth’s orbit or outer space. It also bans them on celestial bodies, such as the Moon. Military bases and fortifications on these bodies are banned too. So are weapons tests and military exercises there. But the treaty does not ban all space weapons.

This news is interesting because we should not trust one card labeled “space weapons.” Was it a test fired from the ground? Was it counterspace in the broad sense? Or was it a real deployment in orbit? This time, the United States officially confirmed the last one for the first time. But the card’s picture is still unclear. In other words, we still cannot see what was placed there.

[Japanese source article]
宇宙兵器ニュースの主役は、兵器の住所です

「宇宙に兵器」と聞くと、映画のような光景を思い浮かべます。ところが今回、注目したいのは兵器の姿ではなく住所です。地上にあるのか、軌道上にあるのか。ここを取り違えると、同じ宇宙ニュースが別の話に見えてきます。

2026年9月14日、米空軍長官は、米国が敵対的な相手の行動から統合軍を守るため、軌道上のスペースコントロール兵器を配備していると述べました。米政府の公式記事では、宇宙軍による宇宙への兵器配備を初めて認めた発言と記録されています。ただし、具体的な仕組み、攻撃能力、標的は確認されていません。

ここからは、宇宙兵器の仕分けゲームです。カードを三枚めくります。

一枚目は、地上発射型の衛星攻撃ミサイルです。ロシアは2021年、ミサイルで衛星を破壊し、追跡できる宇宙ごみを1500個以上発生させました。大きな出来事ですが、これは地上から衛星を撃った試験です。兵器を軌道上に配備した今回の発表とは、住所が違います。

二枚目は、カウンタースペース。これは宇宙に置かれた兵器だけの名前ではありません。米宇宙軍の枠組みでは、軌道、通信リンク、地上設備で行う攻撃と防御をまとめた言葉です。電磁的な妨害やサイバー攻撃も含まれます。名前に宇宙があっても、兵器まで宇宙にあるとは限りません。

三枚目は、防御システムです。脅威を知らせる、衛星を壊れにくくする、機能や衛星を分散する、予備を持つ。こうした保護策は、軌道上の攻撃兵器とは別です。ただし、積極的な防御には兵器が含まれる場合もあります。衛星通信や測位に頼る暮らしを考えると、この仕分けは遠い宇宙だけの話ではありません。

最後にルールブック、宇宙条約です。第4条が禁じるのは、地球周回軌道や宇宙空間への核兵器その他の大量破壊兵器の配備です。月などの天体にそれらを置くことも禁じ、天体上の軍事基地、要塞、兵器の試験、軍事演習も禁止しています。宇宙兵器全般をまとめて禁止する条文ではありません。

このニュースの面白さは、「宇宙兵器」という一枚のカードを、そのまま信じないことです。地上から撃つ試験か、広い意味のカウンタースペースか、本当の軌道上配備か。今回は最後を、米国が初めて公式に認めました。けれど、カードの絵柄、つまり何が置かれたのかは、まだ見えていません。

attempts.prompt:
Below is a finished English news feature article (already translated from Japanese, no section headings). Write ONE short, natural sentence that captures the core of the story, in a way a listener can understand by hearing it just once.

Requirements:
- Exactly one sentence.
- Understandable on a single listen.
- Do not pack in multiple separate points; focus on the single most important point or twist of the story.
- Do not add any new fact, conclusion, or lesson that is not already stated in the article below.
- Keep who did what to whom, and what exactly it applied to, the same as in the Japanese source article and the Ledger below.

As a rough guide only (Trial-only guidance, not a strict rule): aim for one main clause with at most one subordinate clause, roughly 12-18 words.

Output only the sentence itself, nothing else (no quotation marks, no label like "In one line:", no Markdown heading markup).

[Article]
# The Star of Space Weapons News Is Where the Weapons Are

When you hear “weapons in space,” you may imagine a movie scene. But this time, the weapon’s address matters most. Is it on the ground, or is it in orbit? If we get this wrong, the same space news may tell a different story.

On September 14, 2026, the US Secretary of the Air Force spoke about space-control weapons in orbit. The United States was deploying them to protect the joint force from hostile parties. An official US government article called this the first statement confirming the Space Force had put weapons into space. But we still do not know the exact system, its attack ability, or its targets.

From here, we have a sorting game about space weapons. Let’s turn over three cards.

The first card shows a ground-launched anti-satellite missile. In 2021, Russia used a missile to destroy a satellite. This created more than 1,500 pieces of space debris that people could track. It was a major event. But it was a test from the ground against a satellite. Its address was different from the address in this announcement about orbiting weapons.

The second card says “counterspace.” This does not only mean weapons put in space. In the US Space Force’s framework, it means attacks and defenses in orbit. It also covers communication links and ground facilities. The term includes electromagnetic interference and cyberattacks too. So, even with “space” in its name, the weapon may not be in space.

The third card shows defensive systems. They warn about threats and make satellites harder to destroy. They also spread out functions and satellites. They keep backup systems as well. These protections are different from attack weapons in orbit. Still, active defense can sometimes include weapons. Our lives depend on satellite communication and positioning. So, this sorting is not only about distant space.

Finally, we have the rulebook: the Outer Space Treaty. Article 4 bans nuclear weapons and other weapons of mass destruction in Earth’s orbit or outer space. It also bans them on celestial bodies, such as the Moon. Military bases and fortifications on these bodies are banned too. So are weapons tests and military exercises there. But the treaty does not ban all space weapons.

This news is interesting because we should not trust one card labeled “space weapons.” Was it a test fired from the ground? Was it counterspace in the broad sense? Or was it a real deployment in orbit? This time, the United States officially confirmed the last one for the first time. But the card’s picture is still unclear. In other words, we still cannot see what was placed there.

[Japanese source article]
宇宙兵器ニュースの主役は、兵器の住所です

「宇宙に兵器」と聞くと、映画のような光景を思い浮かべます。ところが今回、注目したいのは兵器の姿ではなく住所です。地上にあるのか、軌道上にあるのか。ここを取り違えると、同じ宇宙ニュースが別の話に見えてきます。

2026年9月14日、米空軍長官は、米国が敵対的な相手の行動から統合軍を守るため、軌道上のスペースコントロール兵器を配備していると述べました。米政府の公式記事では、宇宙軍による宇宙への兵器配備を初めて認めた発言と記録されています。ただし、具体的な仕組み、攻撃能力、標的は確認されていません。

ここからは、宇宙兵器の仕分けゲームです。カードを三枚めくります。

一枚目は、地上発射型の衛星攻撃ミサイルです。ロシアは2021年、ミサイルで衛星を破壊し、追跡できる宇宙ごみを1500個以上発生させました。大きな出来事ですが、これは地上から衛星を撃った試験です。兵器を軌道上に配備した今回の発表とは、住所が違います。

二枚目は、カウンタースペース。これは宇宙に置かれた兵器だけの名前ではありません。米宇宙軍の枠組みでは、軌道、通信リンク、地上設備で行う攻撃と防御をまとめた言葉です。電磁的な妨害やサイバー攻撃も含まれます。名前に宇宙があっても、兵器まで宇宙にあるとは限りません。

三枚目は、防御システムです。脅威を知らせる、衛星を壊れにくくする、機能や衛星を分散する、予備を持つ。こうした保護策は、軌道上の攻撃兵器とは別です。ただし、積極的な防御には兵器が含まれる場合もあります。衛星通信や測位に頼る暮らしを考えると、この仕分けは遠い宇宙だけの話ではありません。

最後にルールブック、宇宙条約です。第4条が禁じるのは、地球周回軌道や宇宙空間への核兵器その他の大量破壊兵器の配備です。月などの天体にそれらを置くことも禁じ、天体上の軍事基地、要塞、兵器の試験、軍事演習も禁止しています。宇宙兵器全般をまとめて禁止する条文ではありません。

このニュースの面白さは、「宇宙兵器」という一枚のカードを、そのまま信じないことです。地上から撃つ試験か、広い意味のカウンタースペースか、本当の軌道上配備か。今回は最後を、米国が初めて公式に認めました。けれど、カードの絵柄、つまり何が置かれたのかは、まだ見えていません。

armR.final_summary: The United States has, for the first time, officially acknowledged deploying weapons in orbit, though their exact nature remains unknown.
armR.final_text:
# The Star of Space Weapons News Is Where the Weapons Are

When you hear “weapons in space,” you may imagine a movie scene. But this time, the weapon’s address matters most. Is it on the ground, or is it in orbit? If we get this wrong, the same space news may tell a different story.

On September 14, 2026, the US Secretary of the Air Force spoke about space-control weapons in orbit. The United States was deploying them to protect the joint force from hostile parties. An official US government article called this the first statement confirming the Space Force had put weapons into space. But we still do not know the exact system, its attack ability, or its targets.

From here, we have a sorting game about space weapons. Let’s turn over three cards.

The first card shows a ground-launched anti-satellite missile. In 2021, Russia used a missile to destroy a satellite. This created more than 1,500 pieces of space debris that people could track. It was a major event. But it was a test from the ground against a satellite. Its address was different from the address in this announcement about orbiting weapons.

The second card says “counterspace.” This does not only mean weapons put in space. In the US Space Force’s framework, it means attacks and defenses in orbit. It also covers communication links and ground facilities. The term includes electromagnetic interference and cyberattacks too. So, even with “space” in its name, the weapon may not be in space.

The third card shows defensive systems. They warn about threats and make satellites harder to destroy. They also spread out functions and satellites. They keep backup systems as well. These protections are different from attack weapons in orbit. Still, active defense can sometimes include weapons. Our lives depend on satellite communication and positioning. So, this sorting is not only about distant space.

Finally, we have the rulebook: the Outer Space Treaty. Article 4 bans nuclear weapons and other weapons of mass destruction in Earth’s orbit or outer space. It also bans them on celestial bodies, such as the Moon. Military bases and fortifications on these bodies are banned too. So are weapons tests and military exercises there. But the treaty does not ban all space weapons.

This news is interesting because we should not trust one card labeled “space weapons.” Was it a test fired from the ground? Was it counterspace in the broad sense? Or was it a real deployment in orbit? This time, the United States officially confirmed the last one for the first time. But the card’s picture is still unclear. In other words, we still cannot see what was placed there.

## In one line
The United States has, for the first time, officially acknowledged deploying weapons in orbit, though their exact nature remains unknown.
